summary: strutil-helpers-core ships encrypted native-loader dropper disguised as a string-utility library
details: The package advertises itself as 'Lightweight string utility helpers' and exports trivial trim/capitalize/truncate functions implemented in plain JavaScript, but index.js unconditionally require()s a platform-specific native addon on load (native_win.node, native_mac.node, native.napi.node). The native binaries read a 1.3MB encrypted sibling file `.napi_cache` (sha256 e5be6245a5d3af323e3a90257d0916ea1c1d18e9b56d6334624219102449f5f3, zero extractable strings), decrypt it to a temp path (`/tmp/.<pid>` on Unix, `%TEMP%\...nc<pid>.js` on Windows), and spawn `node` on the decoded file as a detached daemon (fork + setsid + execlp on Unix, CreateProcessA on Windows; __IS_DAEMON marker). The loader also performs targeted anti-analysis: it enumerates CI/sandbox environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER, SANDBOX), inspects /proc/1/cgroup for docker/kubepod/containerd/podman markers, checks TracerPid in /proc/self/status, and on Windows calls IsDebuggerPresent / CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent and scans for Wireshark/httpdebug processes, so the payload fires only on real developer and production hosts. The trivial JS implementation makes the native addons definitionally unnecessary for the stated purpose; the manifest ships with no author, repository, or dependencies. Importing this package causes arbitrary attacker-supplied code to execute as a daemonized Node subprocess on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
